question:
A 58-year-old patient comes to the physician because of progressive pain and swelling of his left calf for the past 2 days. He has no personal or family history of serious illness. He does not smoke or drink alcohol. His last digital rectal examination and colonoscopy at the age of 50 years were normal. His vital signs are within normal limits. He is 183 cm (6 ft) tall and weighs 80 kg (176 lb); BMI is 24 kg/m2. Physical examination shows redness, warmth, and tenderness of the left calf. The circumference of the left lower leg is 4 cm greater than the right. Dorsiflexion of the left foot elicits pain in the ipsilateral calf. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 15 g/dL
Leukocyte count 9000/mm3
Platelet count 190,000/mm3
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate 12 mm/h
Serum
Urea nitrogen 18 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.0 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase 24 U/L
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST, GOT) 12 U/L
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT, GPT) 10 U/L
Urine
Protein negative
RBC 1/hpf
WBC none
Compression ultrasonography with Doppler shows a non-compressible left popliteal vein with a visible 0.5-cm hyperechoic mass and reduced flow. In addition to initiating anticoagulation, which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Progressive pain and swelling of left calf" -> "Physical examination findings: redness, warmth, tenderness of left calf" -> "Left lower leg circumference 4 cm greater than right" -> "Pain with dorsiflexion of left foot" -> "Laboratory studies: normal values for urea nitrogen, creatinine, liver enzymes, and urine analysis" -> "Compression ultrasonography with Doppler: non-compressible left popliteal vein, hyperechoic mass, reduced flow" -> "Diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis (DVT)" -> "Initiating anticoagulation" -> "Next step: Inferior vena cava filter" -> 95%
enhanced_information: The patient presents with signs and symptoms suggestive of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) confirmed by compression ultrasonography. The appropriate next step in management after initiating anticoagulation is the placement of an inferior vena cava filter to prevent pulmonary embolism.
analysis: The core medical principle in this case is the management of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) to prevent complications like pulmonary embolism. The enhanced information supports the placement of an inferior vena cava filter after initiating anticoagulation in patients with DVT to prevent pulmonary embolism. This intervention is crucial in patients with confirmed DVT and high risk for embolization. Colonoscopy, X-ray of the chest, and abdominal ultrasound are not indicated in the acute management of DVT. Streptokinase therapy is not the next step after initiating anticoagulation and placing an inferior vena cava filter.
